passages.title: Dialogue between a mother and her son
passages.instructions: Complete the dialogue between a mother and her son. Choose the mother’s correct answers from the choices given (A–D).
paragraphs: Son: Where have you been, mother?
Son: What have you bought for me?
Son: But why, mother?
Son: From now on I’ll study hard, mother.
Choices given: A. You’re not studying well.  B. Nothing.  C. I went shopping.  D. Then I’ll buy you what you want.

passages.title: We are more than seventy percent water
passages.instructions: Read the passage and answer the questions (41–50) according to the information in the passage.
paragraphs: Water is hydrogen and oxygen. It boils at one hundred degrees centigrade (100˚C) and it freezes at zero degree centigrade (0˚C).

Without water there could be no life on the Earth. There is less water on the other planets than on the earth. Seventy one per cent of the surface of the earth is [line 5] water and more than seventy per cent of our body is water.

The oceans and the rivers of the world contain most of the water. The five oceans and the many seas together have 97.2 per cent. The Pacific Ocean alone is larger than all the land in the world. On the land there are lakes. Many of them are larger than countries the size of Belgium. There are also huge rivers and [line 10] thirty of them are more than two thousand kilometers long.

Water is usually liquid, such as rainwater, or seawater. It can also be solid, such as ice or snow. For example, in Antarctica, the thickness of the ice is about three thousand seven hundred meters. Water can also be a gas or vapour.

Water is always moving. It moves all the time in a cycle. Rain falls to the ground [line 15] from rainclouds. Some of this water goes deep into the earth through rocks and becomes underground water. Some water, as vapour, rises from the earth and makes new clouds. This vapour comes from plants and trees, from the rivers and from the ground. It also comes from the oceans and seas. So, the cycle is complete. The rain falls from clouds, and it rises again to make new clouds.

[line 20] Plants use water to move food from one part of the plant to another, and people use it in many ways. Today very few people in the world have water in their homes. For all the people on this planet water is very important, but two-thirds of them still have to walk to find it.
passages.note: Line numbers (5, 10, 15, 20) as printed. Bold/italic in the paper: them (line 8), Some of this water (line 15).

questions.stem: Dialogue, gap (1). Son: “Where have you been, mother?” Mother: “______”

options.D: Then I’ll buy you what you want.

explanation_steps: “Where have you been?” asks about a place or activity.
“I went shopping.” fits, and the next line (“What have you bought?”) agrees.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations.
questions.explain_simple: He asks where she was. She says: “I went shopping.”
tips: Read the line after the gap as well.

similar_questions.stem: Wife: Where have you been?  Husband: ______  Wife: Did you see the doctor?
explanation_steps: Place + next line about the doctor.

textbook_ref.rule: In a dialogue, the answer must fit the question before it AND the line after it.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations

questions.stem: Dialogue, gap (2). Son: “What have you bought for me?” Mother: “______” Son: “But why, mother?”

options.D: Then I’ll buy you what you want.

explanation_steps: The son’s next words “But why?” show he is surprised and not happy.
So she bought him nothing.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations.
questions.explain_simple: He says “But why?”. So she bought nothing for him.
tips: “But why?” follows a surprising or bad answer.

similar_questions.stem: Girl: Did you bring my shoes?  Brother: ______  Girl: Why not?
explanation_steps: “Why not?” shows the answer was no.

textbook_ref.rule: In a dialogue, the answer must fit the question before it AND the line after it.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations

questions.stem: Dialogue, gap (3). Son: “But why, mother?” Mother: “______” Son: “From now on I’ll study hard, mother.”

options.D: Then I’ll buy you what you want.

explanation_steps: She must give a reason. The son then promises to study hard.
So the reason is: “You’re not studying well.”
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations.
questions.explain_simple: The reason: he does not study well.
tips: “Why?” needs a reason.

similar_questions.stem: Son: Why are you angry?  Father: ______  Son: Sorry, I’ll come early next time.
explanation_steps: The son’s promise matches the reason.

textbook_ref.rule: In a dialogue, the answer must fit the question before it AND the line after it.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations

questions.stem: Dialogue, gap (4). Son: “From now on I’ll study hard, mother.” Mother: “______”

options.D: Then I’ll buy you what you want.

explanation_steps: The son promises; the mother promises a reward: “Then I’ll buy you what you want.”
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations.
questions.explain_simple: He promises to study; she promises a present.
tips: Match each reply to the line just before it.

similar_questions.stem: Pupil: I will clean the class every day.  Teacher: ______

options.A: Then I’ll give you a prize.

explanation_steps: promise → reward.

textbook_ref.rule: In a dialogue, the answer must fit the question before it AND the line after it.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 1 (p. 1–21): conversations

questions.stem: I passed my exam. My mother was happy ______ she bought me some books.
explanation_steps: Two actions that go together (happy + bought books) → and.
“or” is a choice, “but” is a contrast.
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 30, 68, 82, 98–99.
questions.explain_simple: She was happy and she bought books → and.
tips: and = adding; but = contrast; or = choice.

similar_questions.stem: It was sunny ______ we went to the beach.
explanation_steps: and.

textbook_ref.rule: because + reason; so that + purpose; but/however + contrast; and + addition; so + result.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 30, 68, 82, 98–99

questions.stem: Mother: What are you doing?  Son: I ______.
explanation_steps: “What are you doing?” asks about now → present continuous.
I am + verb-ing → I am studying.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 39; English Grade 8, p. 7.
questions.explain_simple: Now → I am studying.
tips: Answer in the same tense as the question.

similar_questions.stem: What is she doing? She ______.
explanation_steps: is cooking.

textbook_ref.rule: Present continuous = am/is/are + verb-ing, for actions happening now.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 39; English Grade 8, p. 7

questions.stem: There are ______ eggs in the basket.
explanation_steps: “eggs” is plural, so “a” and “an” are wrong.
“There are” gives new information, so we use no article: There are eggs in the basket.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 74; English Grade 8, p. 56–58, 204.
questions.explain_simple: Plural and new information → no article.
tips: a/an only with one thing; with a general plural use no article.

similar_questions.stem: There are ______ books on my desk.
explanation_steps: no article.

textbook_ref.rule: Use 'the' for a thing that is the only one (the moon, the sun) or already known; a/an for one thing that is not specific.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 74; English Grade 8, p. 56–58, 204

questions.stem: I ______ my class work. Can I go out?
explanation_steps: The work is done now, and that is why he asks to go out.
Present perfect (have + past participle) shows a finished action with a result now.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 150; English Grade 8, p. 42, 157.
questions.explain_simple: The work is done now → I have finished.
tips: Action just done + result now → have/has + past participle.

similar_questions.stem: I ______ my homework. Can I play now?
explanation_steps: have done.

textbook_ref.rule: Present perfect = have/has + past participle (he has taken). Use has with he/she/it and one person.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 150; English Grade 8, p. 42, 157

questions.stem: Question: Where were you born?  Answer: ______
explanation_steps: “you” in the question → “I” in the answer.
Birth is in the past → I was born.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 134; English Grade 7, p. 145; English Grade 8, p. 12.
questions.explain_simple: “Were you …?” → “I was born …”.
tips: Always: I was born.

similar_questions.stem: Where was your father born?
explanation_steps: He was born.

textbook_ref.rule: Passive = am/is/are/was/were + past participle (Cars are sold). Use it when the doer is not important.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 134; English Grade 7, p. 145; English Grade 8, p. 12

additional_textbook_refs.rule: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Why did you travel?). Short answers repeat the auxiliary: Yes, you can.

questions.stem: Which of the following words can take the prefix un?
explanation_steps: un + happy = unhappy (a real word).
unlaugh, unsad, uncry are not words.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 191–192, 199, 232–234.
questions.explain_simple: Only “unhappy” is a real word.
tips: un- goes with many adjectives: unhappy, unkind, unsafe.

similar_questions.stem: Which word can take the prefix un?
explanation_steps: unkind.

textbook_ref.rule: un-, dis-, in-, im-, il-, ir- mean 'not'; each word takes its own prefix (incorrect, not 'uncorrect').
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 191–192, 199, 232–234

questions.stem: Which word has the wrong plural form?
explanation_steps: The plural of tooth is teeth (irregular).
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 72–95 (spelling: doubling letters, dropping 'e').
questions.explain_simple: tooth → teeth.
tips: Irregular plurals: tooth–teeth, foot–feet, man–men, child–children.

similar_questions.stem: Which plural is wrong?
explanation_steps: foot → feet.

textbook_ref.rule: Learn the spelling of common words; the sound /s/ at the end of a word is often spelt -ce (justice, office).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 72–95 (spelling: doubling letters, dropping 'e')

questions.stem: The girl is ______ than the boy.
explanation_steps: “than” → comparative: taller.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 58; English Grade 7, p. 16, 124; English Grade 8, p. 109.
questions.explain_simple: “than” needs taller.
tips: -er + than.

similar_questions.stem: My bag is ______ than yours.
explanation_steps: heavier.

textbook_ref.rule: Long adjectives: more ... than / the most ...; short adjectives: -er than / the -est. 'not as ... as' means 'less ... than'.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 58; English Grade 7, p. 16, 124; English Grade 8, p. 109

questions.stem: What was the boy doing yesterday evening?
explanation_steps: The question is past continuous (was … doing).
Answer: He was studying.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 175–176.
questions.explain_simple: “was doing” → “was studying”.
tips: Same tense as the question.

similar_questions.stem: What were you doing at 8 pm?
explanation_steps: was reading.

textbook_ref.rule: Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing; it shows an action that was going on at a time in the past.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 175–176

questions.stem: I ______ to Nakfa next month.
explanation_steps: “next month” → future: will go.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 20, 175.
questions.explain_simple: Next month → will go.
tips: Future time word → will.

similar_questions.stem: We ______ the museum next week.
explanation_steps: will visit.

textbook_ref.rule: Future: will + base verb (I will go) or am/is/are going to + base verb.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 20, 175

questions.stem: If you study hard, you ______ the exam.
explanation_steps: First conditional: If + present, will + base verb.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 161; English Grade 8, p. 34, 129.
questions.explain_simple: If you study, you will pass.
tips: If + present → will + verb.

similar_questions.stem: If you eat well, you ______ strong.
explanation_steps: will be.

textbook_ref.rule: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb. Zero conditional (always true): If + present, present. Second: If + past, would + base verb.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 161; English Grade 8, p. 34, 129

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
explanation_steps: Correct: science, social, English, mathematics. Only D is right.
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 72–95 (spelling: doubling letters, dropping 'e').
questions.explain_simple: Only “mathematics” is right.
tips: School subjects: science, social studies, English, mathematics.

similar_questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
explanation_steps: history and citizenship are correct.

textbook_ref.rule: Learn the spelling of common words; the sound /s/ at the end of a word is often spelt -ce (justice, office).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 72–95 (spelling: doubling letters, dropping 'e')

questions.stem: Our Independence Day is celebrated ______ May 24.
explanation_steps: A date → on.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 12; English Grade 8, p. 31, 181.
questions.explain_simple: On + date: on May 24.
tips: on + date; in + month; at + time.

similar_questions.stem: Martyrs’ Day is ______ June 20.
explanation_steps: on.

textbook_ref.rule: Travel: by car/bus/plane; time: at 5 o'clock, on Monday, in June; place: in, on, under, between, next to.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 12; English Grade 8, p. 31, 181

questions.stem: My father ______ our clothes yesterday.
explanation_steps: “yesterday” → past simple: washed.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 72; English Grade 8, p. 7.
questions.explain_simple: Yesterday → washed.
tips: yesterday, last week, ago → past simple.

similar_questions.stem: She ______ a letter yesterday.
explanation_steps: wrote.

textbook_ref.rule: Past simple: verb-ed or irregular past form; questions and negatives use did + base verb (Did he call?).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 72; English Grade 8, p. 7

questions.stem: Fozia is the ______ woman in the village.
explanation_steps: “the … in the village” → superlative. Long adjective → the most beautiful.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 58; English Grade 7, p. 16, 124; English Grade 8, p. 109.
questions.explain_simple: the most beautiful.
tips: Long adjective: the most …

similar_questions.stem: This is the ______ story in the book.
explanation_steps: most interesting.

textbook_ref.rule: Long adjectives: more ... than / the most ...; short adjectives: -er than / the -est. 'not as ... as' means 'less ... than'.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 58; English Grade 7, p. 16, 124; English Grade 8, p. 109

questions.stem: Zahra and Mussie study very hard. ______ always get good marks.
explanation_steps: Zahra and Mussie = two people → They.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 61; English Grade 7, p. 7–8.
questions.explain_simple: Two people → They.
tips: Two or more people → they.

similar_questions.stem: My brother and I play football. ______ play every day.
explanation_steps: my brother and I → we.

textbook_ref.rule: Use an object pronoun (me, him, her, us, them) after a verb or preposition; possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) replace a noun.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 61; English Grade 7, p. 7–8

questions.stem: I didn’t come to school yesterday ______ I was sick.
explanation_steps: “I was sick” is the reason → because.
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 30, 68, 82, 98–99.
questions.explain_simple: The reason: I was sick → because.
tips: because + reason.

similar_questions.stem: She is happy ______ she passed.
explanation_steps: because.

textbook_ref.rule: because + reason; so that + purpose; but/however + contrast; and + addition; so + result.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 30, 68, 82, 98–99

questions.stem: Which of the following is a passive sentence?

options.B: The boy has broken the window.
options.C: The window was broken by the boy.

explanation_steps: A passive sentence has be + past participle, and the thing that receives the action is the subject: The window was broken (by the boy).
A and B are active.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 134; English Grade 7, p. 145; English Grade 8, p. 12.
questions.explain_simple: “The window was broken by the boy” is passive.
tips: Passive: was/were/is/are + past participle (+ by …).

similar_questions.stem: Which sentence is passive?

options.B: The letter was written by Ali.

explanation_steps: was written.

textbook_ref.rule: Passive = am/is/are/was/were + past participle (Cars are sold). Use it when the doer is not important.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 134; English Grade 7, p. 145; English Grade 8, p. 12

questions.stem: ______ you play football in your school?
explanation_steps: you → Do.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 57; English Grade 8, p. 7.
questions.explain_simple: you → Do.
tips: Do + you/we/they.

similar_questions.stem: ______ they speak Tigrigna?
explanation_steps: Do.

textbook_ref.rule: Present simple: he/she/it takes -s (he watches); questions and negatives use do/does + base verb (Does he help?).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 57; English Grade 8, p. 7

additional_textbook_refs.rule: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Why did you travel?). Short answers repeat the auxiliary: Yes, you can.

questions.stem: In which order would these words be written in a dictionary?
explanation_steps: All start with “mo”. Third letter: Monday, money, monkey have n; most has s → most is last.
Fourth letter: Mon-d-ay, mon-e-y, mon-k-ey → d, e, k.
Order: Monday, money, monkey, most.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 32, 41; English Grade 8, p. 101.
questions.explain_simple: d, e, k, then s: Monday, money, monkey, most.
tips: Compare letter by letter until the letters are different.

similar_questions.stem: Dictionary order:
explanation_steps: d, g, k.

textbook_ref.rule: Dictionary order: compare the first letters; if they are the same, compare the second letters, and so on.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 32, 41; English Grade 8, p. 101

questions.stem: The old person is my uncle. ______ is 80 years old.
explanation_steps: uncle = a man → He.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 61; English Grade 7, p. 7–8.
questions.explain_simple: Uncle is a man → He.
tips: man → he; woman → she; thing → it.

similar_questions.stem: My aunt lives in Keren. ______ is a teacher.
explanation_steps: She.

textbook_ref.rule: Use an object pronoun (me, him, her, us, them) after a verb or preposition; possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) replace a noun.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 61; English Grade 7, p. 7–8

questions.stem: How ______ sugar do you add in your tea?
explanation_steps: Sugar is uncountable → How much.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 148, 274–276; English Grade 8, Units 6–7.
questions.explain_simple: Sugar → How much.
tips: How much + uncountable.

similar_questions.stem: How ______ water do you drink?
explanation_steps: much.

textbook_ref.topic: Quantity words (some, any, much, many, too, enough)
textbook_ref.rule: some = an amount with plural or uncountable nouns; too = more than is good; very = a lot; enough = as much as needed.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 148, 274–276; English Grade 8, Units 6–7

questions.stem: My parents ______ to the market everyday.
explanation_steps: “everyday” (= every day) → habit → present simple.
My parents = they → go (no -s).
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 57; English Grade 8, p. 7.
questions.explain_simple: Parents (they) + go.
tips: they + base verb in the present simple.

similar_questions.stem: The children ______ to school every day.
explanation_steps: go.

textbook_ref.rule: Present simple: he/she/it takes -s (he watches); questions and negatives use do/does + base verb (Does he help?).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 57; English Grade 8, p. 7

additional_textbook_refs.rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb (is, has, goes); a plural subject takes a plural verb (are, have, go).

questions.review_flag: Kept as printed: ‘everyday’ should be ‘every day’. Answer not affected.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled wrongly?
explanation_steps: The correct spelling is “exercise”.
Textbook: English Grade 8, p. 72–95 (spelling: doubling letters, dropping 'e').
questions.explain_simple: Right spelling: exercise.
tips: ex-er-cise.

similar_questions.stem: Which word is spelled wrongly?
explanation_steps: answer.

textbook_ref.rule: Learn the spelling of common words; the sound /s/ at the end of a word is often spelt -ce (justice, office).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, p. 72–95 (spelling: doubling letters, dropping 'e')

questions.stem: My hen lays ______ egg everyday. I sell ______ egg in the market.
explanation_steps: First time: one egg, not known → an egg.
Second time: the same egg we just talked about → the egg.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 74; English Grade 8, p. 56–58, 204.
questions.explain_simple: First “an egg”, then “the egg” (the same one).
tips: a/an the first time; the when we speak about it again.

similar_questions.stem: I saw ______ dog. ______ dog was black.
explanation_steps: a first, then the.

textbook_ref.rule: Use 'the' for a thing that is the only one (the moon, the sun) or already known; a/an for one thing that is not specific.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 74; English Grade 8, p. 56–58, 204

questions.stem: Akordet is ______ hot. Sometimes the temperature reaches 45° centigrade.
explanation_steps: We need a word before an adjective that means “a lot”: very hot.
“more hot” needs “than” (and we say hotter); “enough” goes after the adjective (hot enough); “much hot” is wrong.
Textbook: English Grade 6, p. 148, 274–276; English Grade 8, Units 6–7.
questions.explain_simple: 45° is a lot of heat → very hot.
tips: very + adjective.

similar_questions.stem: The mountain is ______ high.
explanation_steps: very high.

textbook_ref.topic: Quantity words (some, any, much, many, too, enough)
textbook_ref.rule: some = an amount with plural or uncountable nouns; too = more than is good; very = a lot; enough = as much as needed.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 6, p. 148, 274–276; English Grade 8, Units 6–7

questions.stem: The rule of the school says, “Every student ______ wear a school uniform.”
explanation_steps: A rule = obligation → must or has to.
“Every student” is singular → has to (correct) and must (correct). So B and C.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 167–168, 187; English Grade 8, Unit 3 (p. 46–71).
questions.explain_simple: Both “has to” and “must” show a rule. So B and C.
tips: Rules: must / has to (singular) / have to (plural).

similar_questions.stem: Every driver ______ carry a licence.
explanation_steps: must and has to both work.

textbook_ref.topic: Modals (must, should, have to, can, may, might)
textbook_ref.rule: Modal verbs (must, should, can, may, might, will) are followed by the base verb without 'to'; have to / ought to keep 'to'.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 167–168, 187; English Grade 8, Unit 3 (p. 46–71)

questions.stem: I asked my father to buy me a mobile telephone, but he <u>rejected</u> my question.
explanation_steps: “but” shows the father did not do what I asked.
reject = not accept.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227.
questions.explain_simple: He said no. Reject = not accept.
tips: “but” tells you the second part is the opposite.

similar_questions.stem: She <u>rejected</u> the offer because the pay was low. ‘Rejected’ means:
explanation_steps: refused.

textbook_ref.rule: Read the whole sentence: the words before and after tell you the meaning of the new word.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227

questions.review_flag: Kept as printed: ‘rejected my question’ (‘request’ is meant). Answer not affected.

questions.stem: He does not have friends and no one likes him, because his <u>conduct</u> is bad.
explanation_steps: People don’t like him because of the way he acts.
conduct = behaviour.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227.
questions.explain_simple: Conduct = the way you act (behaviour).
tips: Ask: what makes people not like you? – your behaviour.

similar_questions.stem: The teacher praised Hana for her good <u>conduct</u>. ‘Conduct’ means:
explanation_steps: behaviour.

textbook_ref.rule: Read the whole sentence: the words before and after tell you the meaning of the new word.

questions.stem: What percent of the surface of the earth is covered by water?
explanation_steps: “Seventy one per cent of the surface of the earth is water.” → 71 per cent.
“more than seventy per cent” in the text is about our BODY; 97.2 per cent is the part of all water that is in the oceans and seas.
But 71 per cent is also, in numbers, “more than 70 per cent”, so D can be defended.
Textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons (e.g. Unit 10, p. 199–220: stories).
questions.explain_simple: The text says 71 per cent of the earth’s surface is water.
tips: Check which thing each number describes.

similar_questions.stem: How much of our body is water?
explanation_steps: “more than seventy per cent of our body”.

textbook_ref.rule: Find the part of the text with the same words as the question; read that sentence carefully.

questions.review_flag: Keyed B (71 per cent, exact words of the text); C ‘more than 70 per cent’ is the text’s figure for the human body, but 71 % is also mathematically ‘more than 70 %’, so D ‘B and C’ is defensible. Both accepted. Teacher decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is true?

options.A: More than half of our body is water.
options.B: More than two- third of people in the world have water in their homes.
